newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LIGHTNING THREAT TEMPORARILY STILLS CHASE AT U.S. OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LIGHTNING THREAT TEMPORARILY STILLS CHASE AT U.S. OPEN.

text.p: The threat of lightning temporarily stilled the chase at Congressional Country Club on Friday as Tom Lehman, Ernie Els and Tiger Woods charged after U.S. Open leader Colin Montgomerie.

Montgomerie, who shot a brilliant five-under-par 65 Thursday to top the 156-man field, was one of some 60 players yet to tee off for the second round when play was suspended at 11:52 a.m. (1552 GMT) because of lightning in the area.

When play was halted, British Open champion Lehman was just one shot off the pace at four under par after a tumultuous round that included four birdies and three bogeys during the 16 holes he completed.
In the steamy-hot early going, the sounds of a Tiger on the prowl also rumbled through Congressional as Masters champion Woods got back into the U.S. Open hunt with four birdies on the front nine.
Woods, whose four-over-par 74 on Thursday had left him a massive nine strokes behind Montgomerie, wasted little time in getting rid of the bad taste of his floundering first-round finish.

The 21-year-old Woods, playing in a group with Lehman, was on target with his irons as he birdied the first, third, fifth and seventh holes -- all from within five feet -- to reach level par for the tournament.
Woods slipped back to one over par with a bogey at the 13th and then posted back-to-back birdies at 14 and 15 before another bogey at 16 dragged him back to even par.

Another contender making a charge was 1994 Open champion Ernie Els. The strapping South African also birdied four holes on the front side to reach three under par. He bogeyed the 10th and parred the next four holes to stand at two-under.
Also joining the chase was journeyman pro Olin Browne, who stood at three under par through 12 holes after starting the day one-over.
Birdies were not available to everyone, of course, on a layout that produced only nine under-par rounds on Thursday.
Steve Stricker, joint second after his first-round 66, double-bogeyed the fourth hole to drop to two under par, where he stood through nine holes.

John Daly, playing his first major championship since undergoing his latest round of treatment for alcoholism, withdrew after nine holes. He had carded three bogeys on the day and stood at 10 over par for the tournament.
Dave Schreyer, fresh from the satellite Hooters Tour, did not have much chance to enjoy the two-under 68 that had left him joint sixth after the first round.
The Georgian started his round Friday with bogey-bogey- double bogey to topple from the leaderboard.
Taking Schreyer's place as an outsider with a hot hand was Scott Dunlap, who matched Woods's brilliant front side of four- under 31.

Dunlap, who has missed eight cuts on the U.S. tour this year, had two more birdies after the turn to haul himself up to one under par after starting the day at five-over. Bogeys at 16 and 18 pushed him back to 66, and one-over for the tournament.
